retrieval_path: MemorySystem.retrieve (http:http://127.0.0.1:8700, policy markdown-notes:vendor-default), one retrieval per question and policy shared by every arm

qa.reader_prompt: LongMemEval step-by-step reading prompt, sessions in date order

versions.resolved_dependencies: uv.lock pins every transitive dependency to markdown-notes's own uv.lock at the tag; prereleases resolved: fastmcp==4.0.0b1 and fastmcp-slim==4.0.0b1 (markdown-notes requires fastmcp==4.0.0b1), opentelemetry-instrumentation==0.63b1 and opentelemetry-semantic-conventions==0.63b1

recipe.notes: documented local install (pip/uv install markdown-notes, SQLite + sqlite-vec). Semantic search is on by default because fastembed and sqlite_vec import (config_models.py _default_semantic_search_enabled). The local reranker jinaai/jina-reranker-v1-tiny-en is configured but reranker_enabled defaults to False (config_models.py:430), and the vendor LoCoMo benchmark does not enable it, so the recipe runs without a reranker. No LLM anywhere in ingest or search: the recipe makes zero provider calls.

common.notes: markdown-notes has no extraction model. The embedder runs through the LiteLLM provider because the built-in openai provider never sends `dimensions` (openai_provider.py embed_documents), so text-embedding-3-large would return 3,072 dimensions; the LiteLLM provider forwards `dimensions` for text-embedding-3 models. Calls go to OPENAI_BASE_URL via semantic_embedding_api_base. markdown-notes keeps its default semantic_min_similarity of 0.55 in this config. text-embedding-3-large scores lower in absolute terms than bge-small: in the 2026-10-05 metered smoke the relevant note scored 0.466 for 'What did Caroline sign up for in May 2023?', so vector search dropped it and the query returned nothing (full-text search did not match either).

capabilities.time_notes: The session date is rendered into the note title, a `session_date` frontmatter field and the heading, exactly where the vendor converter puts it. markdown-notes's own created/updated timestamps are file and index times, not event times. search_notes takes no reference date, so query_time is ignored.

provenance.mechanism: one note per session named <source_id>.md; each search_notes row maps back through its file_path. Rows are whole-note entities (entity_types default), so every item cites exactly one session.

capabilities.delete_notes: delete_note MCP tool on the session's note removes the file and its index rows. Nothing is derived across notes, so no residue is expected.
capabilities.readiness: synchronous: /finish runs `bm reindex --search --embeddings -p <ns>` (the vendor benchmark's command), which returns after full-text indexing and embedding. Completeness is `known` when its summary reports 0 embedding errors and `bm status --json` counts as many files as were written, else `degraded`. The vendor's `bm status --json` readiness poll has no readiness field to read at 0.23.2 (its helper returns None and proceeds).
capabilities.namespace: project: one markdown-notes project per namespace, named <ns>, rooted at /data/notes/<ns>

vendor-default.maps_to: search_notes(page_size=10, search_type='hybrid', output_format='json'): page_size default 10 in search_notes and top_k default 10 in the vendor benchmark; hybrid is the default search type when semantic search is on; semantic_min_similarity 0.55, semantic_vector_k 100, reranker off

fixed-evidence.maps_to: same call with page_size=30, so the harness can pack an 8,000-token budget from more candidates than the default page

deviations_from_vendor_code: Sessions arrive one at a time through /ingest and are written as notes in the vendor converter's format; the vendor converter writes a whole dataset first. Indexing happens at /finish with the vendor's reindex command.

Note ids and titles use the opaque source id (src-...) instead of locomo-cNN-sNN, and the frontmatter drops dataset_id, conversation_id and session_number, which would leak dataset identity across the sanitizer.
The session date is rendered from the ISO event_time into the LoCoMo phrase format ('1:56 pm on 8 May, 2023') for every dataset; the vendor copies LoCoMo's raw string.

Real-time file watching is off (BASIC_MEMORY_INDEX_CHANGES=false) so the warm MCP server never indexes concurrently with the explicit `bm reindex`; indexing still runs only through the vendor's reindex command.
The warm MCP session starts at container start instead of after the first ingest, and serves every project.

Item text is matched_chunk with the note title prefixed when the chunk lacks it, mirroring the vendor's qa.assemble_context header; the vendor's character budget (12,000 chars, 10 hits) is replaced by the harness's shared packer.
The MCP client is an independent implementation (no vendor benchmark code is copied, because the repository is AGPL-3.0).
